wentPoorly: DM-290 attempt 1 was rejected: a throw after a matched comparison left accumulated read-back pages behind (fail-open), stateType was compared case-sensitively against a deny list, and the outcome URL was taken from the read-back unchecked. The ticket body specified the comparison but not what a failed final part must leave behind: a planning gap, not a tier gap.

Two workers wrote into the shared coordinating checkout through relative paths (DM-285 in skills/, DM-295 in headerView.ts). Both reverted it and the orchestrator verified the checkout clean, but other runs share that checkout.
Ticket worktrees after the first had no node_modules; DM-285 symlinked and DM-287 ran npm ci before the orchestrator started cloning node_modules into each worktree.
The host cannot set worker model or effort, so every claim's effort is the planned value, not one applied; tier-fit on effort is nominal for this sprint.

A pre-existing macOS-only failure (acpProcess.test.ts, failing at 88c212f) blocked the Definition of Done test check and was fixed in the acceptance round with a test-fixture change outside the epic's tickets.

Two ticket pointers were off: DM-290's set_epic_status description lives in src/mcp/tools/authoring.ts, and DM-291's 'mutating commands take an idempotencyKey' conflicted with DM-290's no-outer-transaction rule.
wentWell: An adversarial reviewer on DM-290 found a fail-open (stale read-back pages could let a wrong Linear project verify) before acceptance; attempt 2 fixed it with regression tests shown to fail on the old code, and DM-291 turned the constraint into a runtime guard.
All eight row checks passed on the first run, and the parallel DM-289 and DM-290 (both in plans.ts) merged without conflict.
Workers proved their tests were not vacuous by reverting the change under test (DM-289: 8 of 11 fail; DM-290: 9 fail; DM-291 command-path test).
Dev-app screenshots (DM-294, DM-295) ran with an isolated user-data-dir and an inert agent stand-in; the live database stayed at schema 9 throughout the run.

risks: Schema V10: merging this epic migrates every repository database to version 10 on first open, and installed builds at 9 then refuse it. The parallel epics agent-clis and space-scorecards are at 9 today; whichever lands second must renumber if it also adds a migration.
Trust limit: DM cannot read Linear, so verification trusts the agent's read-back. It catches mistakes, not an agent that misreports (recorded in docs/architecture.md).

No real Linear workspace was exercised. The guide assumes Linear's hosted MCP can search by text, list and add relations, move an issue out of a project and (optionally) set sort order; only the fake server proves the flow.

Merge conflicts likely at merge to main: .tsprune-ignore was refreshed (119 entries), and src/main/agents/adapters/acpProcess.test.ts (a macOS-deterministic stderr fixture, outside this epic's tickets) may also be touched by agent-clis.

Portable imports (src/core/repo/importer.ts) write runs and saved revisions without the transfer guard, and transfers are not portable: another machine can start a run or save while a transfer is open here (discovery from DM-289).

Process: two workers briefly wrote into the shared coordinating checkout through relative paths (DM-285 skills/, DM-295 headerView.ts); both were reverted and the checkout verified clean. The orchestrator echoed DM-285's claim token into its own local session transcript once; the attempt has completed.

This run's orchestrator session was launched by the agent from the person-written .mcp.json arguments (--role orchestrator --allow-save) because the host did not mount the server, at the person's explicit instruction to proceed.
content.summary: Sprint 1 met its goal. The role guides and repository rules now apply tests-first and Fireguard only when a plan states them, and every ticket lists its tests (DM-285, DM-286). A person-authorized transfer moves a saved epic to a Linear project in execution order: packet, storage and resume, the run/Save lock, read-back verification that completes the epic with outcome.transfer, commands and MCP tools, the agent guide with its kickoff and `dm transfer linear`, an in-app transfer chat, the epic-workspace UI and a runbook (DM-287 to DM-296). The project Definition of Done passed once on the combined work (8,191 tests; coverage 97.82% lines, 95.23% branches), and the sprint landed on linear-handoff as squashed commit c24cf5e. Every Linear behavior was verified against a fake Linear MCP server; no real Linear workspace was used. DM-290 needed a second attempt after a review found a fail-open in its read-back paging.
